exposure: Nonstress test (NST) results (Type III vs Type I)
Cord-blood gas analyses (pH and base-excess values)
outcome: Cord blood cardiac troponin T (cTnT) levels
Cord blood N-terminal-pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels
cohort: The study included 93 cesarean section deliveries of infants born after 34 + 0/7 gestational week, categorized into groups based on nonstress test results (Type III as study, Type I as control).
finding: Cord blood levels of s100B, CK-MB, cTnT, and proBNP were significantly higher in the non-reassuring (Type III) NST group compared to the reassuring (Type I) NST group, and these markers negatively correlated with Apgar scores and umbilical cord pH.
cross-section timing: At birth, using umbilical cord blood samples and immediate Apgar scores.
birth_weight: Birth weight was comparable between the type I and type III NST groups.
